code='''def transform(grid):
    g=[row[:] for row in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    for r in range(h):
        if r < 2:
            for c in range(w):
                if g[r][c] == 0: g[r][c]=1
            continue
        # The frame is fixed: two background columns, then the colored frame.
        for c in range(min(2,w)):
            if g[r][c] == 0: g[r][c]=1
        if w > 2 and g[r][2] == 0: g[r][2]=4
        if r == 2:
            for c in range(3,w):
                if g[r][c] == 0: g[r][c]=4
            continue
        start=3
        # Infer the row's repeating color sequence from its visible motif cells.
        best=None
        for p in range(2,min(12,w-start)+1):
            groups=[{} for _ in range(p)]
            for c in range(start,w):
                v=g[r][c]
                if v:
                    q=groups[(c-start)%p]
                    q[v]=q.get(v,0)+1
            score=sum(max(q.values(),default=0) for q in groups)
            # Prefer shorter periods when they explain the same number of cells.
            key=(score,-p)
            if best is None or key>best[0]: best=(key,p,groups)
        if best is None: continue
        _,p,groups=best
        for c in range(start,w):
            if g[r][c] == 0:
                q=groups[(c-start)%p]
                if q: g[r][c]=max(q.items(),key=lambda kv:kv[1])[0]
    return g
'''

def parse_block(text, marker, next_marker=None):
    s=text.index(marker)+len(marker)
    if next_marker: s2=text.index(next_marker,s)
    else: s2=text.index('\nSame instance',s)
    lines=[x.strip() for x in text[s:s2].strip().splitlines() if x.strip()]
    return [[int(v) for v in line.split()] for line in lines]

pred=mod.transform(demo_in)
